preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: MIX
  description: To approximately 950 mL non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt, add the
    F/2 nutrient stocks and Trace Metals Solution while stirring.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: Bring the total volume to 1 L with non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt.
- step_number: 3
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Cover and autoclave the medium or filter-sterilize it.
- step_number: 4
  action: MIX
  description: When cooled, add the sterile vitamin stocks.
- step_number: 5
  action: STORE
  description: Store at refrigerator temperature.

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: MIX
  description: To approximately 950 mL non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt, add the
    F/2 nutrient stocks and Trace Metals Solution while stirring.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: Bring the total volume to 1 L with non-pasteurized seawater at 30 ppt.
- step_number: 3
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Cover and autoclave the medium or filter-sterilize it.
- step_number: 4
  action: MIX
  description: When cooled, add the sterile vitamin stocks.
- step_number: 5
  action: STORE
  description: Store at refrigerator temperature.

- name: nitrate_replete_bg11_nostoc_linckia
  description: BG11 nitrate-replete condition used for Nostoc linckia growth and biomass
    productivity comparison with nitrate-free BG110.
  modifications:
  - Use BG11 medium with nitrate present.
  - Compare with BG110 medium lacking nitrate.
  purpose: Capture nitrate-replete BG11 growth evidence for Nostoc linckia.

  - reference: PMID:36550226
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: Cultures grown in BG11 accumulated more cell biomass reaching a dry weight
      of 1.65 ± 0.06 g L-1, compared to 0.92 ± 0.01 g L-1 in BG110 after 240 h of
      culture.
    explanation: Literature evidence reports higher biomass and productivity of Nostoc
      linckia in BG11 than nitrate-free BG110.
- name: bg11_synechococcus_ucp002
  description: BG-11 cultivation condition for unaxenic Synechococcus sp. UCP002 isolated
    from the Peruvian Amazon Basin.
  modifications:
  - Culture Synechococcus sp. UCP002 in BG-11 medium.
  - Use standardized growth-parameter and biochemical-profile measurements.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific BG-11 growth and genome-context evidence for Synechococcus
    sp. UCP002.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:36437912
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: The cyanobacterium was isolated from the Peruvian Amazon Basin region
      and cultured in BG-11 medium.
    explanation: Literature evidence directly states that Synechococcus sp. UCP002
      was cultured in BG-11 medium.
- name: bg11_scenedesmus_obliquus_abc009_photoautotrophic
  description: BG-11 photoautotrophic cultivation condition for the lutein-producing
    algal strain reported as Scenedesmus obliquus ABC-009.
  modifications:
  - Use BG-11 medium under photoautotrophic cultivation.
  - Compare air and 2% CO2 gas conditions.
  purpose: Capture strain-level BG-11 growth evidence for Scenedesmus obliquus ABC-009,
    currently mapped by NCBI to Tetradesmus obliquus.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:34584038
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: photoautotrophic mode using BG-11 medium with air or 2% CO2 and heterotrophic
      mode using YM medium.
    explanation: Literature evidence directly states that strain ABC-009 was evaluated
      under photoautotrophic BG-11 cultivation conditions.

variants:
- name: stl_medium_archaeoglobus_variant
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: STL (sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate) medium, a recognizable Archaeoglobus-type
    defined/complex medium used to grow A. fulgidus VC-16, distinct in formulation
    from the DSM 399 record.
  modifications:
  - 'Base built from a 10x salt solution (per L of 10x: NaCl 178 g, MgSO4 74 g, MgCl2.6H2O
    27.5 g, KCl 3.4 g, NH4Cl 2.5 g; Salt II CaCl2.2H2O 1.4 g; Salt III K2HPO4 1.37
    g) added at 100 ml/L.'
  - PIPES buffer 20 ml of 1 M per L; base medium adjusted to pH 6.7 (Hartzell 1999).
    Reed 2001 variant uses Tris+maleic acid 20 mM each, pH 6.1.
  - 'Carbon/electron donor: sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% (w/v) per L (Hartzell 1999);
    DL-sodium lactate ~22 mM (Reed 2001).'
  - Yeast extract 0.5 g/L (replaceable by Wolfe's vitamin mixture 10 ml/L for defined
    medium).
  - 1000x trace element stock (1 ml/L) incl. Na2EDTA.2H2O, Mn/Co/Zn/Ni/Cu/B/Al/Mo/W/Se/V
    salts; (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 1 ml of 0.2% per L.
  - 'Reductant: Na2S 100 mM + Na2S2O3 200 mM stock added at 0.5% v/v after autoclaving
    (Hartzell); Na2S/Na2S2O3 ~1 mM each (Reed).'
  - Resazurin redox indicator; anaerobic, boiled and N2-sparged; good growth 75-82C
    (Hartzell), 83C in glass carboys (Reed).
  purpose: Capture the STL Archaeoglobus-type medium recipe used for A. fulgidus biofilm
    and enzyme studies as a variant of the DSM 399 parent rather than a duplicate
    medium.
  evidence:

      medium recipe used to maintain A. fulgidus VC-16.

      buffer 20 ml of 1 M, trace element stock 1 ml of 1000x, yeast extract 0.5 g/L,
      sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% per L, pH 6.7; reducing agent Na2S 100 mM / Na2S2O3
      200 mM added 0.5% v/v; good growth at 75-82C.
  - reference: doi:10.1128/jb.183.24.7007-7016.2001
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Reed et al. 2001 (J Bacteriol) reports a modified STL medium 3 for
      A. fulgidus, confirming the STL lineage and giving an alternate buffer/reductant
      variant.
    snippet: cells were grown anaerobically at 83C in glass carboys ... modified sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate
      (STL) medium 3 ... 20 mM Tris plus maleic acid, pH 6.1; DL-sodium lactate 22
      mM; yeast extract 0.5 g/L; Na2S and Na2S2O3 1 mM; resazurin.

    explanation: 'Tarui et al. 2007 (J UOEH) explicitly grows the A. fulgidus type
      strain DSM 4304 in DSM399 Archaeoglobus medium, matching this parent record.
      Conditions: static anaerobic, N2-CO2 4:1, 83C, 2-3 d. | Identifiers: DSM 4304;
      ATCC 49558; strain VC-16'
    snippet: Cells of A. fulgidus DSM4304 (VC-16) were grown statically and anaerobically

variants:
- name: stl_medium_archaeoglobus_variant
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: STL (sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate) medium, a recognizable Archaeoglobus-type
    defined/complex medium used to grow A. fulgidus VC-16, distinct in formulation
    from the DSM 399 record.
  modifications:
  - 'Base built from a 10x salt solution (per L of 10x: NaCl 178 g, MgSO4 74 g, MgCl2.6H2O
    27.5 g, KCl 3.4 g, NH4Cl 2.5 g; Salt II CaCl2.2H2O 1.4 g; Salt III K2HPO4 1.37
    g) added at 100 ml/L.'
  - PIPES buffer 20 ml of 1 M per L; base medium adjusted to pH 6.7 (Hartzell 1999).
    Reed 2001 variant uses Tris+maleic acid 20 mM each, pH 6.1.
  - 'Carbon/electron donor: sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% (w/v) per L (Hartzell 1999);
    DL-sodium lactate ~22 mM (Reed 2001).'
  - Yeast extract 0.5 g/L (replaceable by Wolfe's vitamin mixture 10 ml/L for defined
    medium).
  - 1000x trace element stock (1 ml/L) incl. Na2EDTA.2H2O, Mn/Co/Zn/Ni/Cu/B/Al/Mo/W/Se/V
    salts; (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 1 ml of 0.2% per L.
  - 'Reductant: Na2S 100 mM + Na2S2O3 200 mM stock added at 0.5% v/v after autoclaving
    (Hartzell); Na2S/Na2S2O3 ~1 mM each (Reed).'
  - Resazurin redox indicator; anaerobic, boiled and N2-sparged; good growth 75-82C
    (Hartzell), 83C in glass carboys (Reed).
  purpose: Capture the STL Archaeoglobus-type medium recipe used for A. fulgidus biofilm
    and enzyme studies as a variant of the DSM 399 parent rather than a duplicate
    medium.

      buffer 20 ml of 1 M, trace element stock 1 ml of 1000x, yeast extract 0.5 g/L,
      sodium lactate 7 ml of 30% per L, pH 6.7; reducing agent Na2S 100 mM / Na2S2O3
      200 mM added 0.5% v/v; good growth at 75-82C.

      variant.
    snippet: cells were grown anaerobically at 83C in glass carboys ... modified sulfate-thiosulfate-lactate
      (STL) medium 3 ... 20 mM Tris plus maleic acid, pH 6.1; DL-sodium lactate 22
      mM; yeast extract 0.5 g/L; Na2S and Na2S2O3 1 mM; resazurin.

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients except bicarbonate, cysteine and sulfide. Sparge
    medium with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture for 30 - 45 min to make it anoxic.
    Add and dissolve bicarbonate, adjust pH to 6.5 and dispense medium under 80% H2
    and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials to 30%
    of their volume and autoclave. Add cysteine and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas. Prior to use check pH of complete medium
    and adjust to 6.8 - 7.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: 'Note: After growth has started and the culture is becoming turbid
    add sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to 0.5 - 1 bar overpressure.'
applications:
- Microbial cultivation

preparation_steps:
- step_number: 1
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: Dissolve ingredients except bicarbonate, cysteine and sulfide. Sparge
    medium with 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture for 30 - 45 min to make it anoxic.
    Add and dissolve bicarbonate, adjust pH to 6.5 and dispense medium under 80% H2
    and 20% CO2 gas atmosphere into anoxic Hungate-type tubes or serum vials to 30%
    of their volume and autoclave. Add cysteine and sulfide from sterile anoxic stock
    solutions prepared under 100% N2 gas. Prior to use check pH of complete medium
    and adjust to 6.8 - 7.0, if necessary.
- step_number: 2
  action: MIX
  description: 'Note: After growth has started and the culture is becoming turbid
    add sterile 80% H2 and 20% CO2 gas mixture to 0.5 - 1 bar overpressure.'
applications:
- Microbial cultivation

  description: Aerobic low-sulfate Brock's salts (DSMZ medium 88) formulation used
    by Willard et al. 2024 for a broad set of Sulfolobales. Distinct from the anaerobic
    parent in atmosphere and nitrogen source; grouped here as a derived aerobic variant.
  modifications:

    + NZ-Amine)

    N2 gas phase'

  purpose: Aerobic sulfur-oxidation / comparative physiology cultivation of Sulfolobales
    (A. brierleyi, M. hakonensis, M. prunae, S. ohwakuensis, S. tokodaii).
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1128/mbio.01033-24
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Willard et al. 2024 is the shared source for the aerobic DSM-88 variant
      across these strains.
    snippet: 'All Sulfolobaceae species were grown in a low-sulfate formulation of
      Brock’s Salts (DSM-88 medium) containing:'

        equals0.25g/L already in this parent, so no unsupported MgSO4 reduction/substitution

- name: reduced_anaerobic_mbsy_h2_co2
  relationship: DERIVED_FROM
  description: Reduced anaerobic modified Brock's basal salt medium with yeast extract
    (MBSY) used by Sakai & Kurosawa 2017 for anaerobic growth tests of Sulfodiicoccus
    acidiphilus HS-1T. The genuinely anaerobic member of the DSM 2162 evidence set.
  modifications:
  - Modified Brock's basal salts + 1 g/L yeast extract (MBSY)

  - Headspace H2/CO2 (80:20) at 100 kPa; optional 10 g/L elemental sulfur
  - 65-75C; pH 3.0
  purpose: Anaerobic growth testing of Sulfodiicoccus acidiphilus HS-1T.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1099/ijsem.0.001881
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Sakai & Kurosawa 2017 Methods. Basal MBS recipe cited to another
      reference.

variants:
- name: friis_medium_mycoplasma_hyopneumoniae_isolate_growth
  description: Modified Friis medium condition supporting growth of seven Mycoplasma
    hyopneumoniae isolates measured by ATP luminometry.
  modifications:
  - Use modified Friis medium as described by Friis 1975.
  - Incubate slowly shaken Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae cultures; source reports isolate-dependent
    behavior across five Friis medium batches.
  purpose: Capture isolate-level Mycoplasma hyopneumoniae growth evidence under the
    parent Friis medium record.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:20851152
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: Doubling times (Tds) of the isolates grown in slowly shaken cultures
      varied between 4.8 and 7.8 h.
    explanation: The source directly measured growth kinetics for seven named Mycoplasma
      hyopneumoniae isolates in modified Friis medium, supporting this condition as
      a variant of the Friis parent medium.

    Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 10012.

      L. plantarum ATCC 10012, compared to M 17 medium.
    explanation: The source directly compares growth-associated fermentation performance
      of the two named ATCC strains in MRS versus M17 and then reports oxygen-condition
      doubling times for the same strains.

  description: MRS broth growth optimization condition for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
    BG24, comparing static and shaken cultures and an MRS broth condition adjusted
    to pH 6.5 with additional yeast extract.
  modifications:

variants:
- name: mrs_bsh_oxygen_condition_atcc7050_atcc10012
  description: MRS medium condition used to compare oxygen-level effects on bile salt
    hydrolase production and growth kinetics in Heyndrickxia coagulans ATCC 7050 and
    Lactiplantibacillus plantarum ATCC 10012.
  modifications:
  - Compare MRS medium with M17 medium for bile salt hydrolase production.
  - Evaluate oxygen concentration effects in MRS medium, including anaerobic and microaerophilic
    conditions.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific MRS growth and doubling-time evidence under the
    parent MRS medium record.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:39353547
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: Cultivation of cultures in MRS and M17 media revealed that MRS medium
      enhanced BSH production by 235.98 % in H. coagulans ATCC 7050 and 147.37 % in
      L. plantarum ATCC 10012, compared to M 17 medium.
    explanation: The source directly compares growth-associated fermentation performance
      of the two named ATCC strains in MRS versus M17 and then reports oxygen-condition
      doubling times for the same strains.
  ingredient_mentions:
  - source_label: oxygen
    reported_action: UNSPECIFIED
    stage: MRS oxygen-condition experiments
    source_modification_index: 1
    source_text: Evaluate oxygen concentration effects in MRS medium, including anaerobic
      and microaerophilic conditions.
    reason: Primary abstract supports anaerobic versus microaerophilic comparisons
      but gives no supplied gas species mixture, dose or addition/removal procedure.
      The oxygen condition is not converted into a liquid ingredient event.
    held_fields:
    - OPERATION
    - QUANTITY
    evidence:
    - reference: PMID:39353547

      snippet: varying oxygen concentration levels
      explanation: Primary abstract verifies oxygen-condition comparison only; full
        preparation method unavailable.
- name: mrs_broth_bg24_ph_yeast_extract_optimization
  description: MRS broth growth optimization condition for Lactiplantibacillus plantarum
    BG24, comparing static and shaken cultures and an MRS broth condition adjusted
    to pH 6.5 with additional yeast extract.
  modifications:
  - Compare static culture with 100 rpm and 200 rpm shaking in MRS broth.
  - Compare original MRS broth at pH 5.7 with MRS broth at pH 6.5 enriched with 5
    g/L yeast extract.
  purpose: Capture strain-specific BG24 MRS broth growth optimization evidence under
    the shared MRS parent medium.
  evidence:
  - reference: PMID:38194015
    supports: SUPPORT
    snippet: The specific growth rate of L. plantarum BG24 was 0.416 h-1, the doubling
      time was 1.67 h, and the biomass productivity value was 0.14 gL-1 h-1 in the
      original MRS broth (pH 5.7) while higher values were found as 0.483 h-1, 1.43
      h and 0.17 gL-1 h-1, respectively, in MRS broth (pH 6.5) medium enriched with
      5 g/L yeast extract.
    explanation: The source directly reports quantitative growth kinetics for Lactiplantibacillus
      plantarum BG24 in original and modified MRS broth.

  description: AMS1 alternate-phosphorus utilization experiment in Carini et al. 2014
    Figures 1-2, reconciled against this imported formulation. Composite differences;
    no single relationship enum selected. Parent preserved.
  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.
  - 'No phosphate is added to the alternate-P assay base; omit the phosphate of original
    AMS1 Table 1. This is not a claim of zero residual phosphate: the Figure 2 inoculum
    was previously grown on phosphate.'
  - 'Added ribose 5-phosphate: 1.0 micromolar final, numerically equal to the parent''s
    0.001 millimolar. This supports the assay, not the complete parent recipe. The
    paper does not specify D/L stereochemistry for this phosphorus substrate; do not
    certify the parent''s stereoisomer.'
  - Base preparation follows Carini 2013 Media preparation (inorganic AMS1 autoclaved,
    then carbon-dioxide and air sparging; vitamins and organics added afterward),
    rather than the parent's generic dissolve-all/filter-all steps. Reported base
    pH 7.5-7.7 is not an optimum or a separate measurement of every 2014 assay.
  purpose: Test HTCC7211 utilization of ribose 5-phosphate as an alternate phosphorus
    source.

  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'
  - FeCl3 1 micromolar (parent 117 nanomolar). The AMS1 base source specifies FeCl3.6H2O,
    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'

    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.

    phosphorus source.

  modifications:
  - 'Relative to this imported parent: pyruvate 100 micromolar (parent 1 millimolar);
    glycine 5 micromolar (parent 50 micromolar); methionine 5 micromolar (parent DL-methionine
    50 micromolar). The paper does not resolve methionine stereochemistry.'

    but its 117 nanomolar dose is overridden by the main assay.
  - 'Full vitamin mixture: B1 6 micromolar, B3 800 nanomolar, B5 425 nanomolar, B6
    500 nanomolar, B7 4 nanomolar, B9 4 nanomolar, B12 700 picomolar, myo-inositol
    6 micromolar, 4-aminobenzoate 60 nanomolar. Parent contains only biotin 4 nanomolar
    and thiamine 60 micromolar.'
  - AMS1 Table 1 base uses MgSO4.7H2O at 2.8 millimolar, not parent magnesium sulfate
    28 millimolar. Source hydrate forms also specify CaCl2.2H2O, MnCl2.4H2O, ZnSO4.7H2O,
    CoCl2.6H2O, Na2MoO4.2H2O and NiCl2.6H2O; corresponding parent forms are anhydrous
    or unspecified. Retain Table 1 molar doses for these unchanged-dose salts, without
    mass conversion.

    changes; methionine and serine stereochemistry is not specified in the inspected

    added HMP as HMP-independent growth.'

    sulfate at 28.0 mM. Other unchanged Table 1 base-salt and macronutrient molar
    amounts remain as reported there.

    heptahydrate, cobalt chloride hexahydrate, sodium molybdate dihydrate and nickel
    chloride hexahydrate as specified in Table 1; retain their Table 1 molar amounts
    rather than infer mass equivalents from the local anhydrous or unspecified forms.

    nM; Table 1 specifies the hexahydrate and its basal 117 nM is overridden by the
    assay methods.

      (doi:10.1038/ismej.2014.61) found an HMP requirement and HMP contamination in
      their thiamin stock. Trace HMP in the 2013 batches was not quantified by the
      inspected 2013 paper; do not interpret nominal absence of added HMP as HMP-independent
      growth.'

    xylose, glucose).

  purpose: Capture the explicit modified DSMZ 640 recipe used to isolate and characterize
    T. calidifontis Rx1.

variants:
- name: atcc_1490_base_no_formate_fumarate
  relationship: OMITTED_COMPONENT_VARIANT
  description: ATCC medium 1490 (Modified Chopped Meat medium) used WITHOUT the added
    formate and fumarate of the parent record.
  modifications:
  - Formate and fumarate omitted relative to the parent (ATCC 1490 + formate + fumarate).
  - Base ATCC 1490 Modified Chopped Meat medium; anaerobic, 37C, 24-48 h.
  purpose: Several BV-associated and gut anaerobes are reported on plain ATCC 1490
    without the formate/fumarate supplement; model as the base variant rather than
    asserting growth on the formate+fumarate parent.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1186/1471-2334-11-200
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: O'Hanlon et al. 2011 distinguishes the plain ATCC 1490 base from
      the formate+fumarate parent formulation.
    snippet: Fusobacterium nucleatum ATCC 25586 and Porphyromonas levii ATCC 29147
      were all grown in ATCC medium 1490 (Modified chopped meat medium).
- name: atcc_1490_carbonate_co2_buffered
  relationship: SUPPLEMENTED_VARIANT
  description: ATCC 1490 modified chopped meat medium buffered with carbonate/CO2
    (Johnston et al. 2001).
  modifications:
  - Carbonate/CO2 buffering added to ATCC 1490 base (exact carbonate species/concentration
    and gas composition not printed).
  - For MIC assays, medium clarified through a 0.8 um filter (assay-use processing).
  - Anaerobic glove bag; serum bottle technique; 38C.
  purpose: Capture the carbonate/CO2-buffered ATCC 1490 variant used for Fusobacterium
    necrophorum growth and MIC assays.
  evidence:
  - reference: doi:10.1002/ptr.765
    supports: SUPPORT
    explanation: Johnston et al. 2001; ATCC 1490-derived variant with carbonate/CO2
      buffering; no formate/fumarate, so distinct from the parent.
    snippet: Fusobacterium necrophorum (ATCC 27852) was grown in a modified chopped
      meat medium (ATCC 1490) buffered with carbonate/CO2. For MIC assays, this medium
      was clarified through a 0.8 um filter.

    needed to resolve the reactor concentrations is unavailable. Do not automatically
    divide these parent amounts or import preculture buffering into the reactor. Chemical
    hydrates, stereochemistry, and the generic parent filter-sterilization step remain
    unverified. '

- step_number: 1
  action: ADJUST_PH
  description: Prepare Solution A according to the linked DSMZ 1021 protocol and adjust
    Solution A to pH 8.0. This is not a measured final-medium pH.
- step_number: 2
  action: AUTOCLAVE
  description: For the solid preparation, sterilize Solution A and Solution B separately
    at 121 C for 20 min. Do not autoclave the serum-supplemented mixture.
- step_number: 3
  action: COOL
  description: Cool the separately sterilized solutions to 50 C, then combine A and
    B.
- step_number: 4
  action: MIX
  description: To 4 parts of the combined basal preparation, add 1 part sterile foetal
    or newborn calf serum. Preserve the reported ratio; no fixed serum batch dose
    or mass concentration is asserted.
